715273.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have four customers with open invoices on today's date, named "10 Trucking" (customer A), "2 Trucking" (customer B), "A-1 Towing" (customer C) and "a1 towing" (customer D). Their names differ by a number, a dash or capitals.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name "10 Trucking", type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make invoice for customer A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 100.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  3. Make customer B: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name "2 Trucking", type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  4. Make invoice for customer B: Same way as invoice for customer A, on customer B's page: Fixed Line Total 100.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  5. Make customer C: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name "A-1 Towing", type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  6. Make invoice for customer C: Same way as invoice for customer A, on customer C's page: Fixed Line Total 100.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  7. Make customer D: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name "a1 towing", type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  8. Make invoice for customer D: Same way as invoice for customer A, on customer D's page: Fixed Line Total 100.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.

  • Have four vendors with open bills on today's date, named "10 Trucking" (vendor A), "2 Trucking" (vendor B), "A-1 Towing" (vendor C) and "a1 towing" (vendor D). Their names differ by a number, a dash or capitals.

  1. Make vendor A: Click Parts in the top bar, then Vendors in the left menu, then New Vendor. Type the Name "10 Trucking", pick Credit Terms "Net 30" and Taxes "Exempt (0%)", then click Save & Close.
  2. Make bill for vendor A: Click Parts in the top bar, then Purchase Orders in the left menu, then New PO. Pick vendor A in Vendor.   3. Make vendor B: Click Parts in the top bar, then Vendors in the left menu, then New Vendor. Type the Name "2 Trucking", pick Credit Terms "Net 30" and Taxes "Exempt (0%)", then click Save & Close.
  4. Make bill for vendor B: Same way as bill for vendor A, with vendor B in Vendor: Cost 100.00; type today's date in Invoice Date.
  5. Make vendor C: Click Parts in the top bar, then Vendors in the left menu, then New Vendor. Type the Name "A-1 Towing", pick Credit Terms "Net 30" and Taxes "Exempt (0%)", then click Save & Close.
  6. Make bill for vendor C: Same way as bill for vendor A, with vendor C in Vendor: Cost 100.00; type today's date in Invoice Date.
  7. Make vendor D: Click Parts in the top bar, then Vendors in the left menu, then New Vendor. Type the Name "a1 towing", pick Credit Terms "Net 30" and Taxes "Exempt (0%)", then click Save & Close.
  8. Make bill for vendor D: Same way as bill for vendor A, with vendor D in Vendor: Cost 100.00; type today's date in Invoice Date.

715286.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as a user whose custom role has every permission except "Reports" in the Page Access card.
  • Make sure you have a link to A/R Summary and a link to A/P Detail, copied earlier from the address bar by an Admin user.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open the ShopView home page.

Setup

  1. Make the role for this test: Click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Settings, then Roles & Permissions in the left menu, then Create Custom Role. In "Choose a template" click Admin, then Apply. Type a Role Name, then switch off "Reports" in the Page Access card, then click Create.
  2. Sign in with that role: Click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Settings, then Staff in the left menu. On the row "Tech ShopView" click the edit icon; in Edit Staff Member pick the new role in Role and click Save & Close. Then click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Logout, and on the QA site's sign-in page click Tech in the quick login panel. After the test, sign in as Admin again and set Tech ShopView's Role back to Technician.
715286.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • None of the six reports is offered (on screen: "A/R Aging Summary", "A/R Aging Detail", "A/R Aging Collection", "A/P Aging Summary", "A/P Aging Detail", "A/P Unpaid Invoices"), as today.

Step 2:

  • The A/R Summary link shows in the address bar.

Step 3:

  • The report does not open, as today for a user without this permission.

Step 4:

  • The A/P Detail link shows in the address bar.

Step 5:

  • The report does not open, as today.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • S1-N1: “If the user lacks 'Reports → Page Access', the reports are not available, as today.”
  • Key Decisions, Permissions: “Permissions. Viewing all six reports, and exporting them, is governed by 'Reports → Page Access', unchanged. No new permission is introduced and no existing permission changes. Opening a document from a report uses the permission that already opens that document (see Story 7). The credit term on the A/R Collection call list follows the customer card's rule: only users with the 'View and Manage AP/AR Data' switch see it, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV (Story 9). Amounts show to everyone who can open the reports, as today and as on Sales By Customer and Inventory Value; 'See Financial Data' does not hide them.”

Partly checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026; not yet seen on that build: signing in as Tech ShopView after giving it another role.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). The design draws no picture of this behaviour (all 7 boards and 45 figures checked); the case follows the PRD.

AUTOMATION: READY

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a customer with an unused credit memo, credit memo A, and an unused deposit, deposit A, both dated the same earlier day, date A.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with only that customer ticked in the Customer filter.

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make credit memo A: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type the date 5 days before today in Credit Date, type 50.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.
  3. Make deposit A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, click Save, and close the New Line window. Open the Finance tab and click Add Deposit; in Create Deposit pick a Payment Method and type 41.00 in Deposit Amount, then click Record Deposit. Open the Lines tab and click New Line; in the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 1.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Leave Invoice Date as today, click Create Invoice, and reload the page (F5) when the New Customer Payment window opens. The invoice is paid from the deposit, and the rest, 40.00, stays as an unused deposit dated today.
1062566.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The report reloads for date A.

Step 2:

  • Credit memo A and deposit A are listed in this bucket: a credit dated exactly on the as-of date is Current.

Step 3:

  • The report reloads for the day after date A, with every bucket collapsed.

Step 4:

  • Credit memo A and deposit A are now listed here, one day past their own date, and no longer in "Current".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows)

  • S1-R5a: “A document is Current when its due date is on or after the as-of date. Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". This is how QuickBooks ages them (SV-11441).”
  • S1-R5: “A/R Detail and A/P Detail keep their aging buckets in this fixed order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current". Inside each bucket, rows open in customer or vendor name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4), ties by document number (S2-R4).”
  • S4-N1: “Changing the as-of date, the customer or vendor filter, the Past due filter or the Location filter collapses every group, as changing the date or filter does today.”

Partly checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026; not yet seen on that build: an unused deposit dated an earlier day (the part of a deposit left over is dated the day its invoice is made).

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), version of 5 Nov 2026 (1793886208-34e0), read 10 Nov 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html); page 3 "Collapse all and pinned group rows" (board Grouped.dc.html). The design draws no picture of this behaviour (all 7 boards and 45 figures checked); the case follows the PRD.

AUTOMATION: READY

1062567.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a vendor with an unused vendor credit, vendor credit A, dated an earlier day, date A.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/P Detail (Reports, then "A/P Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with only that vendor ticked in the Vendor filter.

Setup

  1. Make vendor A: Click Parts in the top bar, then Vendors in the left menu, then New Vendor. Type a new Name for vendor A, pick Credit Terms "Net 30" and Taxes "Exempt (0%)", then click Save & Close.
  2. Make a bill for vendor A to return a part from: Click Parts in the top bar, then Purchase Orders in the left menu, then New PO. Pick vendor A in Vendor. In Part Number type a new part number and click "Add new special order part: …"; type a Description, 1 in Quantity and 500.00 in Cost; click Add, then Save & Close. In the Purchase Orders list click Receive on that order (Vendor column: vendor A); type a Vendor Invoice # (for example "a bill for vendor A to return a part from"), type today's date in Invoice Date, type 0 in Tax, then click Receive Parts (1).
  3. Make vendor credit A: Click Parts in the top bar, then Returns in the left menu, then Create Return. Pick vendor A in Vendor, type a Packaging Slip, pick the part received on a bill for vendor A to return a part from in Part Number, type 50.00 in Price Per Unit, then click Save Return. In the Returns list tick that return and click Receive Credit; type a Credit Memo Number, type the date 5 days before today in Credit Date, type 0 in Tax, then click Post Credit.
1062567.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The report reloads for date A.

Step 2:

  • Vendor credit A is listed in this bucket.
  • Its Due Date is date A, its own date.
  • Its Past Due reads 0.

Step 3:

  • The report reloads for the day after date A, with every bucket collapsed.

Step 4:

  • Vendor credit A is now listed here, with Past Due 1, and no longer in "Current".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R5a: “A document is Current when its due date is on or after the as-of date. Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". This is how QuickBooks ages them (SV-11441).”
  • S2-R6: “A blank value (for example a vendor credit on A/P Unpaid Invoices, which has no due date and no Past Due) sorts to the bottom of its group in both directions. On A/P Detail a vendor credit shows its own date as its due date, as today, so it is not blank there.”

715391.custom_expected:

  • Vendor credit B shows location A (the vendor's location for that credit, where it was entered, as today).

Step 2:

Step 3:

A vendor has no single location of its own: each bill or credit is written to the vendor's account at one location, and that is the location it shows (tech plan, 21 Oct 2026).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R7: “Choosing locations narrows every row, group, subtotal, total, page count, sort and export to the open documents at those locations. A row belongs to the location of its own document. On A/R: the invoice, credit memo or deposit. On A/P: a bill belongs to the location of the delivery it was received on; a vendor credit from a vendor return belongs to that return's location; any other vendor credit keeps its vendor's location, as today. That is the location the Location column shows.”

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

With a Past due filter they can differ: a Summary keeps the whole row of a customer or vendor that qualifies (Current and credits included), while a Detail report lists only the invoices or bills that qualify, plus every credit.”

On A/R: the invoice, credit memo or deposit. Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • Key Decisions, Permissions: “Permissions. Viewing all six reports, and exporting them, is governed by 'Reports → Page Access', unchanged. The credit term on the A/R Collection call list follows the customer card's rule: only users with the 'View and Manage AP/AR Data' switch see it, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV (Story 9). Setup

  1. Locations to use: Use "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" as location A (it comes first in A to Z order) and "Staging Lethbridge - 4310" as location B.   3. Make bill 1: Click Parts in the top bar, then Purchase Orders in the left menu, then New PO. Pick vendor A in Vendor. In Part Number type a new part number and click "Add new special order part: …"; type a Description, 1 in Quantity and 300.00 in Cost; click Add, then Save & Close.   4. Make bill 2: While switched to location B (see "Locations to use"): Same way as bill 1, with vendor A in Vendor: Cost 200.00; type today's date in Invoice Date.
  5. Make vendor credit 1: Click Parts in the top bar, then Returns in the left menu, then Create Return. Pick vendor A in Vendor, type a Packaging Slip, pick the part received on bill 1 in Part Number, type 50.00 in Price Per Unit, then click Save Return. In the Returns list tick that return and click Receive Credit; type a Credit Memo Number, type today's date in Credit Date, type 0 in Tax, then click Post Credit.

  • The dialog closes.

Step 4:

  • The page switches to dark theme.

  • The dialog opens again and is readable in dark theme.

What you should see today: in step 1, the right-hand button of the "Switch location?" dialog reads "Switch Location" with a capital L instead of "Switch location". · If it fails in a DIFFERENT way from what is described above, that is a NEW problem — please report it.

· If it PASSES, the fix has shipped: report it so the ticket can be closed and this note removed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11537 (Story 7, Document links open where they can)

Switch your active location to view it?" (for a part sale: "This part sale is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?"), buttons "Cancel" on the left and "Switch location" on the right, and a close × at the top right.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Click a part sale at another enrolled location | "This part sale is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?" | Same dialog”
  • Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. Nothing new is drawn. Basis: d-reuse-existing-pattern.”
